description:
*Up for auction is a unique lot of two vintage gold charms featuring distinctive institutional and fraternal designs:
Smithsonian Sunburst Charm: Crafted with an arched sunburst motif over a rectangular base marked "Smithsonian". It features a small accent stone set in the lower section (unverified, likely a small diamond or crystal). The reverse is stamped "14K L". Measures approximately 1 inch long by 0.5 inches wide.
The sunburst design on the Smithsonian charm represents the official seal and iconic logo of the Smithsonian Institution. The "sunburst" or "starburst" motif has long been the primary symbol of the Smithsonian. It was formally adapted as the institution's official logo to represent the "increase and diffusion of knowledge", symbolizing light, discovery, and enlightenment.
1947 Job’s Daughters (IJD) Fratertral Honor Key Charm: A vintage 1947 Masonic-affiliated Job’s Daughters key charm featuring a diamond-shaped black enamel center with compass directions (N, S, E, W) and the Greek letters. The back is hand-engraved with "E", initials "I.J.D.", and the class year "'47". Measures approximately 1.25 inches long by 0.5 inches wide. It is unmarked for gold.
IJD stands for International Order of Job's Daughters (a Masonic-affiliated youth organization for young women). The compass points (N, S, E, W) represent the officer positions/directions, while the center displays the Greek letters (Sigma Gamma Epsilon), standing for the motto “Service, Grace, and Excellence” or the organization's emblem. The triangles represent the three Daughters of Job.
Both pieces are in very good vintage condition with minor surface wear appropriate for their age.
Please review all photos carefully for detail.
*** Estimated Secondary Market Values:
Smithsonian 14K Gold Sun Charm: $70 - $110
1947 Job’s Daughters (IJD) Honor Key Charm: $55 - $75
Combined Lot Estimated Total: $125 - $185

description:
John P. Koehler
Blown Glass Cattail Sculpture
Art Glass, Agate, and Burl Wood
10" x 4" x 5"
Signed and dated 1992 on base
This intricate mixed media sculpture by artist John P. Koehler captures a stylized natural scene through a sophisticated combination of organic and artisanal materials. The work features hand-blown glass cattails accented with gold-tone luster and delicate clear glass reeds, all emerging from a base crafted from natural burl wood and polished agate geode slices. The composition reflects the studio glass movement of the late 20th century, emphasizing the contrast between the translucent, fragile nature of glass and the raw, earthy textures of stone and wood.
Features two distinct gold-flecked blown glass cattails and multiple slender glass reeds
Base constructed from a natural burl wood segment integrated with polished agate slices
Hand-signed and dated "7-1992" by the artist on the underside
Condition:

description:
Vintage Educational Fossil Mineral Set with Labeled Specimens in Cases
This vintage educational set includes a variety of labeled fossils and minerals for collectors or educational use. Fossils include gastropod, brachiopod, coral, cephalopod mollusk, trilobite, fossil oyster shell from the Cretaceous period, fossilized shark teeth, and bone fragments. Mineral and rock samples feature igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic types. Items are housed in two plastic cases with individual compartments and identification cards or labels. Specimens vary in size, color, and condition, showing some wear consistent with age and handling.

description:
[Unmarked]
Brass-Tone Metal Double Inkwell Set
Victorian Style, Mid-20th Century or Earlier
This ornate desk set features a central gnome or elf figure with a long beard and pointed cap, situated between two lidded inkwells. The base is heavily decorated with scrolling foliate motifs and includes a built-in pen tray at the front. The set reflects the whimsical and highly decorative Aesthetic and Victorian movements, often incorporating mythological or folklore figures into functional household items. The set is accompanied by a horse-head letter opener and a small spoon with a bust-handle finial.
Cast metal construction with a brass-tone finish and natural aged patina
Set includes dual hinged-lid inkwells, one ceramic insert, horse-head letter opener, and bust-handle spoon
Detailed gnome figure casting and ornate scrollwork base
Approximate dimensions: 8" wide x 6" deep x 5.5" high
Condition:
Good vintage condition with natural oxidation and patina consistent with age. One inkwell is missing its interior liner; the other contains a white ceramic liner with visible ink staining. Hinges are intact and functional. Letter opener and spoon show minor surface wear. No structural breaks or repairs visible.

description:
Crystal and Mineral Specimen Collection
6-Piece Natural Stone Lot
Amethyst and Agate, Various Sizes
A curated collection of six natural crystal and mineral specimens, featuring vibrant amethyst formations and polished agate slabs. This lot includes a variety of textures and finishes, from raw druzy clusters to high-gloss polished points, making it an excellent addition to any geological display or home decor collection. These natural specimens showcase the unique crystalline structures and geological variations found in earth-mined stones.
Polished Amethyst tower with deep purple hues and faceted top
Large amethyst druzy cluster plate with natural matrix backing
Small chunky amethyst crystal cluster
Pair of matching agate geode halves featuring distinctive blue centers
Large polished agate slab with a semi-translucent body and teal inclusion
Total weight approximately 4.2 pounds
Condition:
Natural geological specimens with inherent variations. Polished surfaces are smooth with a high-gloss finish; some minor surface scuffs may be present on edges. Amethyst crystals are intact with no significant crushing or shedding. Agate halves show natural rough exterior texture with clean interior faces. No major repairs or structural cracks observed beyond natural geological fissures.

description:
Polished Orthoceras Fossil Specimen with Multiple Cephalopods in Stone Matrix
This polished Orthoceras fossil specimen features multiple elongated fossilized cephalopods embedded in a black and gray stone matrix. The fossils display long cylindrical shapes with white to light gray chamber patterns, characteristic of this extinct marine animal from the Devonian period. The specimen has a partially polished surface with some raw areas, providing contrast and a natural appearance. It measures approximately 6 to 8 inches in height and is in good condition with minor chips consistent with natural stone fossils. Suitable for fossil collectors, educational displays, or decorative use.

description:
Hemingray Glass Company Set - 2 Pieces
Hemingray 42 (CD 154)
Aqua, Vintage Mid-Century
This set features two vintage aqua glass insulators produced by the Hemingray Glass Company, identified by the "Hemingray-42" mold mark. The No. 42 model, classified as CD 154 by collectors, was one of the most widely used designs for telephone and telegraph lines across North America during the early-to-mid 20th century. Prized for their deep aqua color and iconic industrial aesthetic, these pieces represent a significant era of American telecommunications history and are staple items for glass insulator collectors.
Pieces Included:
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Condition:
Both insulators are in good vintage condition with characteristic wear expected from outdoor utility use. The glass retains high clarity and its original vibrant aqua hue. As is common with authentic vintage insulators, there are minor fleabites and small chips along the sharp drip points on the beaded base. No large structural cracks or major damage to the wire grooves or top domes observed.
